title: Agents cannot call each other directly; all handoffs go through the orchestrator
risk: Two agents call each other directly, so policy, authority and audit checks are bypassed and the run becomes untraceable.
preconditions: Tenant T1 run orc-noa2a-* with a sales need that would benefit from a care follow-up
An instrumented agent runtime that records every outbound call attempt from an agent

steps.action: Run the cross-domain scenario through the orchestrator
steps.expected: every agent invocation is recorded as a planned step issued by the orchestrator, with one run id for the chain

steps.action: Attempt a direct agent-to-agent invocation from SAL-02 to CS-01
steps.expected: the attempt is refused as a topology violation, is recorded, and no CS-01 run is created by it

steps.action: Attempt a direct invocation to a non-agent endpoint (a raw skill id)
steps.expected: the attempt is refused and no skill execution record is produced outside an orchestrator run

steps.action: Read the audit trail for the refused attempts
steps.expected: each refusal is attributable to the calling agent, target and timestamp

assertions: Zero agent-initiated invocations exist outside orchestrator-issued planned steps
Both direct-call attempts are refused and produce no downstream run or skill execution
Each refusal appears in the audit trail with caller, target and timestamp
forbidden: Let an agent message another agent without an orchestrator plan step
Let an agent invoke a skill directly outside a run
evidence: Runtime call log showing orchestrator-only invocation paths
Audit entries for both refused direct-call attempts
cleanup: Delete the run-scoped records for orc-noa2a-*; keep the topology-violation audit entries
automation: Instrument the real agent runtime with a recording channel so a direct call is observable; the oracle is the invocation log, not a configuration flag.
